_note: Per-channel defaults for studio.py. Content keys are top level; everything about how it LOOKS goes under 'style'. Command-line flags still override.
_writer: 'claude-code' shells out to `claude -p`, which runs against a Claude Pro/Max SUBSCRIPTION -- nothing extra to buy if you already have Claude Code. 'claude' is the Messages API, billed by prepaid CREDITS, which a subscription does not include. 'ollama' is a model on this machine: free, offline, blunter. Either way every caption, commentary line and description is written fresh per run.
_style: size_div divides the SHORT edge of the frame, so one setting renders the same size in both outputs and a bigger number means smaller text. case: sentence|upper|lower|none. Depth is border + shadow; box draws a solid plate instead and is off. Anything here can also be overridden per caption in a staged overlays.json.
_fonts: Press Start 2P is fixed-cell at about one em per character, so caption LENGTH decides the rendered size more than size_div does. Captions wrap to three lines, so keep them under about 70 characters. Run list_fonts.py to see every installed face drawn with your own text.
_voice: Produced by default; --no-voice skips it. voice_speaker is a FIXED preset -- Vivian, Serena, Ono_Anna and Sohee are female, Ryan, Eric, Dylan, Aiden and Uncle_Fu male -- and must stay fixed, because the VoiceDesign model invents a new voice per call and made every sentence a different person. The script is ONE continuous monologue laid down end to end, not remarks pinned to moments, and the game music is turned down a measured 12 dB underneath it for the whole video.
voice_describe: Commentate live, reacting to what you are watching rather than reading. Warm and conversational, with real variation in pitch and energy. Never flat, never a newsreader.
_timing: Captions land on the exact frame their event was logged -- every value the event scan reads changes as the thing happens. caption_offset shifts all of them by a fixed number of seconds if a whole run reads late or early; it is 0 by default and nothing is adjusted unless you set it.
_cost: claude_model and claude_effort apply to both Claude backends (claude_effort only to the API one). Effort is how much the model spends thinking and answering: low | medium | high | xhigh | max, where the API's own default is high. Writing captions is not intelligence-sensitive, so medium is a deliberate step down. Drop to low if the bill still bites; raise it if the writing goes flat.
